summary: When Nora opens an Instagram post, reel or story, she now sees what each photo and video shows, not just the caption and a list of links.
details: Each item comes back with a short description of what is in it, read the same way she reads a picture or a clip sent in the chat, and the caption sits beside those descriptions. She can compare what the poster wrote with what the post actually shows, and answer from both, without a second step per item.

The caption is never used to steer what she looks for. It is the poster's own words, and a post could use it to make her misread the pictures, so the pictures are read on their own and she puts the two side by side herself.
Opening the same post again is quick and free: what she saw the first time is remembered by the picture or clip itself.
Profiles and account searches read no pictures and look exactly as they did.
limitations: Only the first 8 items of a post are looked at, four at a time. The rest are still listed, and she can look at any of them on request.

A slow item does not hold the rest up. If a video takes too long, or cannot be read, that item says so and everything else still comes back. If none of the items can be seen, she says she could not see the post rather than describing it from its caption.
As before, she only opens a story, post or reel when someone in the conversation asks her to.
